I energize the primary with 120v AC with a 12 watt light bulb in series giving a 1200 Ohm resistance on the primary side. It's a bit laughable I suppose but I see no reason why it wouldn't work, even if it is on a tiny scale. Basically, we all have pressure and flow at our disposal in our homes. The idea is simply this: Attach a turbine or dynamo to the house mains water supply, so whenever you turn on a tap you generate electricity, thus taking advantage of the flow of energy that's already there, rather than just letting it literally go down the drain. My fav lil motor: YouTube - PMH pulse motor.AVI 2 x 8wrap coils on a common 'U' shaped iron core. 6 little neo magnets(n,s,n,s,n,s,n,s) on a VCR spindal and a getto fab reed switch/hall sensor. I say reed/hall because the switch contacts physically like a reed switch, but since it has a tiny magnet on it that repulse one magnet and attracts the next one....it acts like a hall sensor and only turns the switch on when a S magnet passes.
